speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health what safeguards exist to ensure access to polyclinic care for seniors aged 65 years and above who (i) cannot go online to book appointments and (ii) repeatedly find that online slots are already fully booked.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Health whether it is possible to release polyclinic next-day appointment slots in a few fixed tranches each day rather than have a single release of time slots at 10.00 pm.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the written questions by Dr Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our healthcare system is facing increasing demands, as our people age and need more healthcare, including primary care.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At the same time, the completion of new polyclinics that were planned had been delayed due to the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As a result, some polyclinics have greater demand and less easy availability of appointments.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Pending the development of new polyclinics, they are putting in place short-term measures to address this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To do so, non-urgent cases may be given an appointment for another day or advised to seek treatment at a nearby Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) general practitioner (GP) clinic.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Polyclinics will also try to leverage telemedicine as much as possible and contract private GPs to help deliver the service.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents, especially seniors who are worried about the experience of the polyclinic booking system.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: One resident tried to make an online booking for her elderly mother – four days in a row, logged in at the booking time, could not get a slot.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Another senior, not IT-savvy, cannot go online, went to a polyclinic, was told to book online.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State two supplementary questions?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to explore the role of things like hotlines and other ways to improve our processes so that the appointments and the services available at the polyclinics are indeed more accessible and more user-friendly, especially to seniors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The question of subsidies at the CHAS GP clinics and how they relate to the charges and the costs at the polyclinics is an important one.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As Dr Tan knows and as Members know, this is something we are constantly reviewing, on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will have to constantly review the conditions as well as the level of subsidy that we provide for the CHAS GP clinics and indeed, taking into account the relationship with what happens on the polyclinics.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I want to echo what Dr Tan Wu Meng has said.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I do continue to receive feedback from our seniors who have said it is almost impossible to make an online appointment at the polyclinic run by National University Health System (NUHS) at Bukit Panjang.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State whether we are able to set aside some walk-in appointment slots, especially for the seniors so that they do not have to go through that online booking?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Notwithstanding MOH having built new polyclinics with increased capacity, why is it the case that we are still not able to meet the demand?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do indeed set aside a proportion of the slots for walk-in appointments.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, not all the appointment slots at a given polyclinic, on a given day, are only for online appointments.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are slots that are set aside for walk-in patients.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The potential walk-in patients are assessed and so, sometimes, they will be given advice to come back on another day or to seek help at a GP clinic, depending on what it is they present with.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Recently, in the news, we had the Khatib and Sembawang Polyclinics' timings talked about.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But there is also an increasing demand as our population ages and the aged have increasing frailty and co-morbidities that will require further care.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is a combination of growing demand and the projected supply having been constrained by the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are trying our best to catch up and provide more services to increase our capacity.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just to the Senior Minister of State on this point again, is it possible to increase the number of walk-in slots at the polyclinics in view of the feedback that many Members of this House are receiving from seniors who have difficulties in accessing the online system and making a booking?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also give us an indication of the percentage of these slots which are walk-in slots?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The other supplementary question pertains to the number of feedback MOH has received on complaints of not being able to book a slot through the online system.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Senior Minister of State have some numbers for us, so we can understand the extent of the problem?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not have the data to answer his second question; that was not part of the Parliamentary Question that was filed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would point out that that does not change the overall capacity available at the polyclinics.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is actually the heart of the issue.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I understand there is frustration with the online system for seniors, but there are also people who are able to use the online system and as a result, the availability of the resources and the capacity for the services at the polyclinics are better matched to those patients.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It means that the clinical notes are available ahead of time, preparations can be made ahead of time for investigations, tests and the allied health services that support, given the instance of someone coming down to the polyclinic.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I think we have to have a balance.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If we went to a fully walk-in system, that would have an implication on the ability for the care teams to deliver the service that they are used to delivering.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The question then is, what is the best way of determining that balance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a result of the difficulties in booking polyclinic slots, how many senior patients have gone to the Accident and Emergency (A&E) Departments at the hospitals for non-emergency cases?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not have the data for the first question that he has asked.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is possible that we are unable to get the data because what he is asking for is those who have not booked, how to track them.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would be happy to try and fulfil but I do not have the data with me today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are happy to explore how we can leverage on other types of resources to be able to help people have better access and utilisation of services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I will work with the teams to explore the use of that suggestion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Like many others who have shared in this House, Sengkang residents have had significant difficulties getting online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To a Parliamentary Question that was filed in March earlier this year, some of our residents are waiting as much as 2.5 hours on the long tail.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One question that I wonder in terms of increasing the number of walk-in slots – what the Leader of the Opposition said earlier – is if we could channel more of those that are currently booking online toward telemedicine options.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The reason behind that is, of course, those who are sophisticated enough to book online, may be also much more comfortable with addressing a telemedicine option.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Related to this, one reason why many younger and more Internet-savvy patients tend to go toward the polyclinics is because there is still a discrepancy between for some employers what is recognised to be a valid medical certificate (MC) – whether you need a polyclinic MC versus a regular GP MC.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand this falls a little bit beyond the remit of the MOH and more on the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Nevertheless, I wonder if this is something that can be explored a little further in terms of guidelines that the Government offers toward allowing for MCs that are across a wider range of providers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think we leave it to the professional teams in terms of how they assess the referral information, the patient demographic, as well as the presenting problems as to which patients can be dealt with an online consultation and which patients will need an in-person appointment.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think that is something for a clinical judgement, rather than a policy position.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we will support the teams so that we can optimise the use of telemedicine and make sure that we improve the capacity available at the polyclinics.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I also declare that I am a medical doctor at a public hospital.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: My first additional supplementary question relates to Mr Yip Hon Weng's query about patients who could not make a booking but later on sought A&E care.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It is not the full data set but that could be a way to analyse this.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Because the polyclinics are very busy, our healthcare brothers and sisters are at the front lines; and we have to support them to do their best as well, for the patients and for the community.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But as I have explained, I do not have that data with me.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I wanted to answer Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's point.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: All medical certificates, medical leave of absence, so long as they are issued by a licensed medical practitioner in Singapore, will be recognised.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I hope that answers the Member's earlier point.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I will move on to answer the hon Member of Parliament Mr Melvin Yong's question.
